people.name: Mahant Surendra Das
people.photoAlt: Mahant Surendra Das of Bandwar Thakurbari
people.notableFor: Served Bandwar Thakurbari for over 40 years and preserved the 200+ year old Krishna Janmashtami Mela
people.journey: Born in 1965 in Khamhar, he left home at the tender age of 13 to become an ascetic (baal sant) and went to Ayodhya. In 1985, he arrived in Bandwar with his guru (a panda from Ayodhya) to receive bhiksha. Captivated by the temple and the village, he chose to stay and devoted over 40 years of his life to the service of the deity at Bandwar Thakurbari.
people.bio: The revered Mahant of the historic Bandwar Thakurbari in Begusarai. A baal sant who left home at 13 and reached Bandwar in 1985 with his Ayodhya-based guru, he served the temple and its deity for over four decades. Under his stewardship, the Thakurbari's 200+ year old Krishna Janmashtami Mela continued to flourish. He passed away on 29 October 2026, leaving behind a legacy of devotion, simplicity, and cultural preservation.

people.name: Dr. Armaan Anand Singh
people.photoAlt: Dr. Armaan Anand Singh, Professor and Author from Bandwar
people.notableFor: Hindi professor at G.D. College, Begusarai, and author of the poetry collection 'Neend Jise Raat Bhar Nahin Aati'. Known for his literary contributions and active role in local educational and cultural initiatives.
people.journey: Dr. Armaan Anand Singh is a Hindi professor at G.D. College (Ganesh Dutt College) in Begusarai. He is also the Nodal Coordinator for the District Extension Centre and the head of the college's Cultural Committee (Sanskriti Prakoshth). As an author, he published a poetry collection titled 'Neend Jise Raat Bhar Nahin Aati'. His poems often explore themes of love, reality, and social commentary, and he has been described as a poet of 'Ganga-Jamuni tehzeeb'. His work has been featured on the 'Vishwa Hindi Sahitya' blog.
people.bio: Dr. Armaan Anand Singh is a prominent academic and literary figure from Bandwar in the Begusarai district of Bihar. He serves as a professor in the Hindi Department of G.D. College, Begusarai, and has held significant administrative roles, including Nodal Coordinator of the District Extension Centre. As an author, his poetry collection 'Neend Jise Raat Bhar Nahin Aati' reflects deep emotional and realistic themes. He is actively involved in organizing cultural and literary events, contributing significantly to the educational and cultural landscape of the region.

people.name: Ramchandra Singh
people.photoAlt: Ramchandra Singh, Freedom Fighter and Martyr from Bandwar
people.notableFor: One of the six students martyred in the police firing at Begusarai on 26 January 1931 during India's freedom struggle. The Shaheed Ramchandra Dwar in Bandwar is named in his honour.
people.journey: Ramchandra Singh, a native of Vandwar (Bandwar) in Begusarai, was among the six students killed in police firing at Begusarai on 26 January 1931 during India's freedom movement. His sacrifice is remembered in local history, and the Shaheed Ramchandra Dwar in Bandwar stands as a memorial to his martyrdom.
people.bio: Ramchandra Singh was a freedom fighter and martyr from Vandwar (Bandwar) in Begusarai district, Bihar. He was one of the six students martyred in the police firing at Begusarai on 26 January 1931 during the Indian freedom struggle. His legacy is preserved in the village through the Shaheed Ramchandra Dwar, a memorial gateway built in his honour, which remains a symbol of Bandwar's contribution to India's independence movement.

people.name: Satyam Bharti
people.photoAlt: Satyam Bharti, Author and Poet from Bandwar
people.notableFor: Author of the ghazal collection 'Suno Sadanira', which received the Ravinesh Kumar Verma Smriti Samman; also published the doha collection 'Bikhar Rahe Pratiman'.
people.journey: Satyam Bharti, born on 11 December 1996 in Vandwar (Bandwar), is a young Hindi author and poet. His ghazal collection 'Suno Sadanira' earned him the Ravinesh Kumar Verma Smriti Samman. He has also published a collection of dohas titled 'Bikhar Rahe Pratiman'. He resides in Ward No. 4 of Bandwar.
people.bio: Satyam Bharti is a young Hindi author and poet from Vandwar (Bandwar) in Begusarai district, Bihar. Born on 11 December 1996, he has made a mark in Hindi literature with his ghazal collection 'Suno Sadanira', which received the Ravinesh Kumar Verma Smriti Samman. He has also published a doha collection titled 'Bikhar Rahe Pratiman'. A resident of Ward No. 4 in Bandwar, he represents the village's vibrant literary tradition.
